title: Model Foundations and Inference Systems

weeks.focus: Derive tensor, probability, token, attention, compute, memory, quality, and cost models; freeze predictions
Build and verify tokenization, tensor operations, causal attention, a tiny transformer, and a loopback streaming server
Break and measure memory, scheduling, overload, cache, precision, and provider assumptions
Decide inference architecture, defend ownership and operating limits, assess, teach, and remediate

readiness_note: Ready after portable lab tests, six isolated evaluator records, deterministic calibration checking, semantic and resource review, and focused and full-course validation passed on 2026-08-03.

outcomes.statement: Derive vectors, matrices, norms, probability, entropy, gradients, and scaled dot-product attention with explicit shapes, units, and numerical limits.
Implement versioned tokenization, embeddings, causal attention, and a deterministic tiny transformer inference path.
Calculate weights, activations, KV cache, bandwidth, concurrency, headroom, failover reserve, and cost per useful output.
Measure queue-inclusive TTFT, inter-token latency, prefill, decode, outcomes, throughput, memory, and profiler limits.
Implement bounded batching, pre-admission resource reservation, quotas, shedding, and traffic-class fairness.
Apply versioned prefix and semantic caches and precision changes without crossing privacy, compatibility, or quality boundaries.
Diagnose memory exhaustion, mixed-length interference, queue overload, cache collision, precision loss, and provider failure from preserved evidence.
Defend an inference architecture across quality, latency, availability, security, cost, ownership, migration, rollback, and reversal.

resources.title: Deep Learning: Chapters 2-4 bounded sections
resources.author_or_publisher: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville / MIT Press
resources.purpose: Ground linear algebra, probability, entropy, gradients, and numerical stability used in local derivations.
resources.assignment: Read Chapter 2 Sections 2.1-2.5, Chapter 3 Sections 3.1-3.4 and 3.13, and Chapter 4 Sections 4.1-4.3; reproduce one matrix, entropy, and gradient calculation.

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need
resources.purpose: Connect the local attention implementation to the original transformer mechanism and notation.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 3.1-3.5 only; annotate tensor shapes, scaling, masking, and parallelism claims.

resources.title: CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
resources.purpose: Reinforce tokenization, resource accounting, architectures, hardware, and current inference-system reasoning.
resources.assignment: Use only Lectures 1-5 and 10 materials; separate token, operator, memory, hardware, and serving claims in a concept ledger.

resources.title: CS336 Lecture 10: Inference
resources.purpose: Visualize prefill, decode, batching, and serving trade-offs with a written equivalent.
resources.assignment: Watch with captions; produce a prefill/decode/batching map and two claims that do not transfer to the Atlas portable CPU lab.

resources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
resources.purpose: Study KV-cache allocation, fragmentation, batching, scheduling, and their workload assumptions.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 2-4 and 7; reproduce the fragmentation argument and list the assumptions that differ from Atlas.

resources.title: Optimization and Tuning
resources.purpose: Compare current preemption, chunked-prefill, and input-processing controls with the local scheduler model.
resources.assignment: Read preemption, chunked prefill, and input processing only; map each current control to the Atlas failure it could affect.

resources.title: PyTorch Profiler
resources.purpose: Define timing, shape, memory, warm-up, and trace-export evidence for the optional adapter.
resources.assignment: Read timing, memory, trace, and long-running sections; write the Atlas measured-profile procedure and its overhead boundary.

resources.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
resources.purpose: Tie numerical representation changes to both hardware efficiency and protected quality evidence.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 1-4 and 5.3-5.5; identify the precision, hardware, corpus, and metric boundaries behind each claim.

resources.title: Taming the tail utilization of ads inference at Meta scale
resources.purpose: Examine operator evidence connecting tail utilization, capacity, reliability, and user latency.
resources.assignment: Read the full case; separate measurements, interventions, outcomes, scale assumptions, and claims that do not transfer to generative Atlas workloads.

failure_experiments.scenario: KV and activation growth exceeds reserved memory
failure_experiments.evidence: same-input broken/repaired hashes, full memory ledger, pre-admission reservation, rejection, headroom, OOM count, and I01
same arrivals and lengths, per-class queue-inclusive TTFT/ITL, chunking/share control, batch progress, and I02-I04

failure_experiments.scenario: arrival rate overloads an unbounded queue
failure_experiments.evidence: open-loop arrival identity, queue maximum, rejection, deadline outcomes, recovery, useful work, and I03

failure_experiments.scenario: prefix or semantic cache survives tenant or version change
failure_experiments.evidence: two pseudonymous tenants, complete identity fields, version/authorization invalidation, cross-tenant and stale hits, and I05-I06

failure_experiments.scenario: reduced precision exceeds the declared quality tolerance
failure_experiments.evidence: reference corpus hash, maximum logit error, top-k agreement, task score, rollout/rollback gate, and I07

failure_experiments.scenario: provider loss amplifies deadlines, attempts, and cost
failure_experiments.evidence: one request identity and deadline, attempts, duplicate work, compatibility/data boundary, fallback capacity, cost, and I08-I10
